test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Directions: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the reported speech.**

The old man said to her, “Good luck to you! May you succeed in your venture!”

options.text: The old man wished you good luck and prayed that you might succeed in your venture.
The old man wished her good luck and prayed that she might succeed in her venture.
The old man exclaimed good luck to you and wished that she may succeed in her venture.
The old man told her good luck and prayed that may she succeed in her venture.

solution:
The correct answer is **The old man wished her good luck and prayed that she might succeed in her venture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
 
 
• The exclamation mark (!) is removed, 'that' is added and the full stop (.) is added in place of the exclamation mark.
 
• For **direct speech to indirect speech**, the reporting verb of an **optative sentence (expressing desire, prayer, wish)** is **changed in** indirect narration into **pray, wish, yearn for, long for, desire, etc**.
 
• **For example:**
 
 
• 
 
**Direct:** *I said to him, "May you be happy."*

 
**Indirect:** *I wished that he might be happy.*

 
 
• 
 
**Direct:** *Mother said to me, "May God bless you."*

 
**Indirect:** *Mother prayed that God might bless me.*

 
 
 
 
• The second-person pronoun ''you'' becomes the third-person pronoun ''she'' and the second-person pronoun ''your'' becomes the third-person pronoun ''her''.
 
• The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (May) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (might) + Object'.
 
• From the given options the only suitable answer is option 3.

 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• You may think that the first option should be the correct option but in the option, the second person pronoun remains unchanged. 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is option 2.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:-

 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1+ing+ Object)

 Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)
